newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PRESS DIGEST - Israel - May 9. [CORRECTED 7:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Israel - May 9. [CORRECTED 7:40 GMT]

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bank Leumi 20 percent share offering set for this month.
- Israel's Tadiran to make alkaline batteries in Jordan.
- Air force demands purchase of more strategic-range warplanes.
- Senior U.S. sources say President Bill Clinton fears confrontation with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over a freeze of Jewish settlement would ignite conflict with Congress and American Jewry.
- Israel's Peled Commission recommends cancelling TV license fees and starting a new commercial channel in 1999.
- Army Intelligence chief Moshe Yaalon says Hamas command in Damascus linked to attack on Apropo Cafe in Tel Aviv. (Corrects title and name of source).
- Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai: "Israeli army needs another two billion shekels -- to close the gaps".
- Gallup Poll: Overwhelming majority favour former Foreign Minister Ehud Barak for Labour party leader. Surprisingly, rival Yossi Beilin of Labour also would beat Netanyahu, 42-40 percent.
- Treasury proposes tax on vehicles entering city centres.
- Southern army commander Shlomo Yanai: "30 Palestinian policemen will lie dead at Netzarim junction if there is a confrontation."
